+  -> EventOps.EventTaskCompletionCommand
+  -> EventOperationsM (Headers '[Header "Cache-Control" Text] EventOps.EventTaskCompletionOutcomeDTO)

+  action `catchError` (\failure -> throwError failure
+    { errHeaders = ("Cache-Control", "private, no-store") : errHeaders failure })

+CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION event_operation_fence_authorization_change()
+RETURNS trigger
+LANGUAGE plpgsql
+SECURITY INVOKER
+SET search_path = public, pg_temp
+AS $$
+DECLARE target_event_id BIGINT;
+BEGIN
+  IF TG_OP = 'UPDATE' THEN
+    IF NEW.id <> OLD.id OR NEW.event_id <> OLD.event_id THEN
+      RAISE EXCEPTION 'authorization identity/event is immutable; revoke and issue explicitly'
+        USING ERRCODE = '23514';
+    END IF;
+    IF TG_TABLE_NAME = 'event_operation_grant' THEN
+      IF NEW.grantee_party_id <> OLD.grantee_party_id THEN
+        RAISE EXCEPTION 'grant recipient is immutable; revoke and issue explicitly' USING ERRCODE = '23514';
+      END IF;
+    ELSIF NEW.party_id <> OLD.party_id THEN
+      RAISE EXCEPTION 'relationship party is immutable; revoke and issue explicitly' USING ERRCODE = '23514';
+    END IF;
+  END IF;
+  target_event_id := CASE WHEN TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN OLD.event_id ELSE NEW.event_id END;
+  UPDATE event_operation_event_state
+    SET authorization_version = authorization_version + 1
+    WHERE event_id = target_event_id;
+  IF TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN RETURN OLD; ELSE RETURN NEW; END IF;
+END
+$$;

Provider refreshes previously replaced canonical event fields and the entire metadata object, erasing editorial corrections. Imports now retain field ownership evidence, refresh unchanged fields, and permanently relinquish edited fields. issue.body:
Consolidates fan-club and event-moment engagement into one capability-gated interaction layer for web and mobile. Reactions, transactional counts, cursor-paginated comments/replies, tombstones, stable mentions, owner policies, scoped moderation, blocking, notification preferences and exact discussion links share server authorization and persistence. Existing engagement IDs and URLs remain compatible; legacy writers delegate to the canonical model after an atomic, audited conversion.

Covered publications: club posts/memories, events/moments, recordings/sessions, record releases, artist releases, classifieds/opportunities and published directory profiles. Attached media shares its publication's discussion. Imported artist social-sync records remain disabled without explicit publication authority. Owners may hide/restore comments but gain no administrator removal or report-decision powers. Privacy, current source permissions, blocking, suspension and revision checks remain authoritative.

The manifest has **159 immutable migrations**: the 116 current-main entries, then eight social compatibility prerequisites and 35 interaction migrations. Integration with main's event-ingestion PR #469 preserves both CI/release gates, SQL bytes and original introduction commits. Activation validates and converts nonempty legacy engagement and permanently fences legacy writes in one transaction. Emergency pause serializes with admitted commands and delivery while preserving authorized canonical reads. Recovery repairs forward without reopening old writers or overwriting accepted writes.

- Existing club reactions remain available before first activation through an explicit, non-cacheable server response. Ordinary authorization/not-found errors and converted pauses cannot enable legacy UI.
- Recordings, sessions and record releases require membership in matching active/published editorial collections. Moderation does not bypass publication. Comments serialize with membership deletion and collection withdrawal; hidden discussions retain their engagement for republication.

- Published record links outside the first 200 feed members or without a preview resolve through one authorized detail lookup. Existing discussions remain reachable without making feed position/media availability a publication grant. Ordinary browsing continues to exclude unavailable-media cards.

- Refreshing a feed now reselects the linked item when its index crosses a page boundary. Unchanged selection preserves user pagination. Five rendered source-kind cases and five real-browser configurations prove both movement directions, exact focus and bounded rendering.
- Classifieds/opportunities require strictly future expiry, matching the existing public detail endpoint. Null/current/past expiry deny summaries, writes, registration and links for ordinary users and moderators; renewal restores existing identities/counts without changing source or engagement data. The pre-fix regression failed; SQL and real HTTP regressions pass.

The final hidden-root finding targeted a superseded pagination function: actual HTTP tests on the existing schema prove redacted hidden roots, visible descendants/counts, all sorts, cursor reply pages and deep links for anonymous/owner/author/ordinary viewers, plus disappearance of empty placeholders. No code change was needed. Validation: the exact repository audit-ci configuration passes. Four local address cases reproduce the vulnerable behavior on 10.3.1 and pass on 10.7.2 (IPv6 link-local and local-use NAT64); two public-address controls remain public. Only version, resolved URL and integrity differ in package-lock.json. No deployment was manually triggered. Independent approval and current-head hosted checks are required before merge.

Sources: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rpw4-54j3-4h4q and https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-2vr4-cq9g-pvrc.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Enforce read-only access with database privileges**

When `production_access.py inventory` receives SQL containing `SET default_transaction_read_only=off` or an explicit read-write transaction, this session default can be overridden because `psql` connects as the `postgres` superuser. Since the CLI forwards arbitrary stdin, an erroneous or repurposed invocation can mutate the live production database despite the helper's read-only contract; execute through a genuinely read-only database role rather than relying solely on `PGOPTIONS`.

A raw client can submit a report reason containing only tabs or newlines because PostgreSQL's one-argument `btrim` removes ordinary spaces but not those characters. The report is accepted and appears in moderation queues with an empty-looking explanation; the same validation is reused for hide, remove, restore, and report-resolution reasons. Apply the all-whitespace test already introduced for comment bodies to these required reason fields as well.
